messages:
Carmen Rivera: Hey team, escalated from Support — customer (acct: acme-inc) is seeing intermittent 401s when calling our /v1/generate endpoint with signed JWTs. They say it works ~95% of the time but fails for some requests. Ticket 89421. Attached logs show 'invalid signature' and also 'token expired' for same user session.

Tobias Klein: @Carmen can you paste a sample of the failing auth header (redact sig)? also which signing library are they using?

Carmen Rivera: They sent this snippet, redacted: `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImtleS0yIn0....`

Carmen Rivera: From logs: `auth: verify_jwt failed: signature verification failed (kid mismatch)` and at other times `verify_jwt failed: token expired by 9s`.

Alex Morgan: Kid mismatch + sporadic expiry sounds like JWKS caching + clock skew. Are they using our hosted JWKS endpoint directly or caching it locally?

Priya Singh: They said their infra caches the JWKS with a long TTL (10m). They rotate keys every 2m for their signer (internal practice). That would explain kid not found. Also short clock skew could cause expiry.

Jamie Chen: Did we recently roll our JWKS? any blips in jwks-cache invalidation in our runtime? Eng-bot, any alerts?

eng-bot: [deploy] jwks-cache-service v1.3.2 deployed at 1965431200. No errors reported in last 3h.

Tobias Klein: Ok. Two separate root causes possible: (A) client's aggressive key rotation + long JWKS cache = kid missing -> signature fails. (B) client's clocks out of sync -> borderline exp/nbf failures. We should reproduce. Carmen can we get a sample failing token and the public JWKS snapshot they used?

Carmen Rivera: Sent both to private. Also attached curl repro from them: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
They say runs 100x, ~5 times it fails.

Alex Morgan: I'll try to reproduce locally by simulating fast key rotation and JWKS TTL. Quick notes for folks: our verifier flow is: fetch JWKS -> cache by issuer for TTL (default 5m) -> use `kid` lookup -> verify. If `kid` absent we fallback to re-fetch once. We do not re-fetch more than once per request to avoid thundering herd.

Alex Morgan: Repro steps I'm going to run: spin a minimal signer that rotates keys every 90s and set the jwks TTL to 5m on our verifier to match their client's setup. See if we hit intermittent 401s.

Priya Singh: Also add clock skew simulation: shift signer time +8s occasionally. Some JWT libs use `leeway=0` by default. That can cause expiry failures. We should test with leeway=0 and leeway=10s.

Jamie Chen: Quick mitigation for customer: ask them to reduce JWKS cache TTL to < rotation period (or better: cache with a short TTL and exponential backoff), and add leeway to their verification (e.g., allow 30s). In parallel we can add telemetry to our verifier to log when we hit kid-miss and when we re-fetch.

Tobias Klein: Agreed. For short-term workaround, we can implement a fast path: when `kid` not found, trigger a synchronous JWKS refresh and retry verif once (we already do one fetch but maybe it was recently cached stale). But careful about perf/DoS. Need rate limiting on refresh for same issuer.

Alex Morgan: I tried the local repro. Steps:
1) Start signer that publishes JWKS with rotating kid every 90s.
2) Configure verifier JWKS TTL = 5m, allow single refetch on kid-miss.
3) Send 500 requests with new tokens.

Result: ~4% of requests got `invalid signature`. Stacktrace: `kid not found in cached jwks -> attempted re-fetch -> race -> still not found if rotation happened between fetch and parse`.

Alex Morgan: Root cause is a race when a key is rotated while a request is in-flight: our cached JWKS may be valid for prior tokens but rotation means the kid exists in the new JWKS but not the one we have; if rotation happens twice in quick succession we can miss. Their signer rotates quickly enough to trigger a window where no snapshot contained the kid used by token.

Priya Singh: Also saw expiration failures in logs when server time skewed by <10s. Customer time drift -> some tokens issued with `exp` too close to now.

Tobias Klein: Proposed fixes:
- Short term (support guidance): ask customer to increase JWKS TTL < rotation window OR slow rotation, and add validation leeway (e.g., 30s).
- Medium: on our side, implement: 1) jittered background refreshes to reduce stale window, 2) when `kid` missing trigger synchronous refresh + single retry with per-issuer cooldown to prevent abuse, 3) log kid-miss metrics (issuer,kid,request id) for visibility.
- Long term: support JWKS delta endpoints or push notifications for key rotation (webhook) so signers announce new keys.

Jamie Chen: Also add an incident note to docs: 'If you rotate keys faster than your JWKS TTL, you can see intermittent 401s due to kid not found.' Keep it short with config examples.

Carmen Rivera: Customer accepted short-term guidance and will slow rotation and add 60s leeway. They asked if we can do an emergency config change while they test.

Tobias Klein: We can enable an opt-in quick-refresh feature for that account: set per-issuer `sync_refresh_on_kid_miss=true` with cooldown 30s. I'll open an internal change with `eng-releases` and tag @Alex for review.

Alex Morgan: I'll prepare a small patch and load test the path. Also add unit tests for fast double-rotation scenario.

eng-bot: [cherry-pick] created PR #1248 for jwks sync-refresh feature at 1965432400.

Carmen Rivera: I'll update the ticket and let the customer know. Thanks all. :pray:

Priya Singh: Follow-up: we should also surface clearer error messages to customers: distinguish `kid not found` vs `signature invalid` vs `expired` in docs so they can triage faster.

Tobias Klein: Agreed. I'll file a small docs task. Closing loop once PR is merged and customer verifies.

Carmen Rivera: last note — customer provided their clock drift logs; they had NTP jitter causing up to 12s drift during maintenance windows. I'll add that to the ticket.

Alex Morgan: Good catch. Recommend they run `ntpdate` or switch to systemd-timesyncd and add monitoring alert if drift >5s.

Carmen Rivera: thread complete for now.
